title.narrative: GLA II - IUCN NL - DRC

description.narrative:
The DRC programme of the Green Livelihoods Alliance focuses on the restoration, protection and sustainable management of the ecosystems in the Virunga and Kahuzi-Biega landscapes. It’s about natural resource management in a sustainable, concerted and inclusive manner, which guarantees the livelihoods of local communities and indigenous peoples and the stability of protected areas.
The programme adopts three envisaged pathways of change:
- Restoring social peace and stability in the East landscape: local communities and indigenous populations in the Virunga and Kahuzi Biega landscapes are acting freely, responsibly and are reconciled. Activities to achieve this include: education of youth, women and land chiefs in sustainable management of natural resources, meetings with the traditional leaders and bringing different stakeholders in the landscape together.
-Re-establishing social and environmental justice: establishment of an environmental juridical clinic providing legal support and strengthened advocacy for the restoration of state authority in the Virunga landscape, so that stakeholders adopt best practices in their daily lives, livelihoods are improved and the living conditions of the local population and indigenous populations have increased.
-Assuring the sustainable use of natural resources and restoring ecosystems: benefits of protected areas should contribute to the sustainable development of local populations, stakeholders are involved in decisions making process and new alternatives are developed.

title.narrative: SCS3 # of times that CSOs succeed in creating space for CSO demands and positions through agenda setting, influencing the debate and/or creating space to engage.

description.narrative: This result shows # of times that CSOs succeed in creating space for CSO demands and positions through agenda setting, influencing the debate and/or creating space to engage, as result of GLA efforts

title.narrative: # of advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs, for, by or with their membership/constituency

description.narrative: Measures the advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs, for, by or with their membership/constituency at national and international level

comment.narrative: At the beginning of the GLA2 programme no spaces were created to engage at national and international level as a result of for CSO engagement in the programme

CSOs succeeded in creating space for CSO demands and positions through agenda setting, influencing the debate and/or creating space to engage at national and international level 9 times. For example: In 2022, we started activities to mobilise CSOs to follow up on the implementation of the recommendations of the universal periodic review. It is through this process that we have created a space to collect input from IPLCs and to involve them in the decision making process by formulating recommendations in relation to their rights as communities and on natural resources.

The aim of the programme is to increase the level of influence or participation in decision making by CSOs and IPLCs in more processes. In addition, the programme aims to increase the level of participation by women and young women/men in all processes. No specific target is defined in this case.

description.narrative: Measures the advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs, for, by or with their membership/constituency at sub-national

CSOs succeeded in creating space for CSO demands and positions through agenda setting, influencing the debate and/or creating space to engage at sub national level 10 times. For example: changing the industry to reduce deforestation by encouraging the construction of houses with bricks instead of wood and make business, especially the mining industry, more conscious about the impact of their activities on nature. FCPEEP encourages them to subsidise women and youth organisations to re-plant what has been destroyed and to encourage community forestry areas. See https://fcpeep-rdc.org/emission-radios-sur-la-protection-des-aires-proteges-et-de-lenvironnement-dans-le-cadre-de-la-gouvernance-forestiere-autour-du-paysage-pnkb/

The aim of the programme is to increase the level of influence or participation in decision making by CSOs and IPLCs in more processes. In addition, the programme aims to increase the level of participation by women and young women/men in all processes. No specific target is defined in this case.

comment.narrative: At the beginning of the GLA2 programme no laws have been blocked, adopted, improved for sustainable and inclusive development as a result of CSO engagement

1 law was blocked, adopted, improved for sustainable and inclusive development as a result of CSO engagement at midline. In 2021 and 2022, CSOs have organized meetings with senators and deputies as the proposition of law 22/030 of the 15th of July 2022 (promoting and protecting the rights of Pygmy indigenous peoples) was going to be examined by the Senate and the Parliament. The CSOs were able to bring the perspectives of the communities they represent, and particularly the women and youth who are even more marginalized because of intersecting discriminations. This successful lobby led to the adoption and promulgation of the law. It finally came into effect in February 2023.
